data.cultural_impact: The name "Samihi" holds a significant impact in Islamic culture as it signifies a healer or one who is wise and intelligent. In Islamic society, the role of healers is highly respected as they are considered to be close to God due to their ability to alleviate physical and emotional pain. Samihi, being a name associated with healing, connotes the idea of someone who is nurturing and compassionate towards others.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Samihi" also holds immense spiritual significance, as it is derived from the Arabic word "Samah," which means "to ease the sufferings of others." In Islamic teachings, alleviating the pain of others is seen as an act of worship that pleases God. Thus, the name "Samihi" suggests an individual who is not only spiritually enlightened but also compassionate towards others, continually striving to ease their suffering and bring them comfort.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Al-Futuh, p. 208-215. The name Samihi carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name Samihi is mentioned in connection with the early Islamic conquests of Egypt and Nubia. Samihi was a Christian bishop of Asyut in Upper Egypt who was converted to Islam by the Arab conqueror Amr ibn al-As. After his conversion, Samihi played a key role in the Islamic conquest of Nubia, serving as an interpreter and adviser to Amr.

historical_references.context: Samihi is mentioned in Ibn Hawqal's description of Egypt as the name of a prominent Islamic scholar and Sufi saint from Asyut. He was known for his learning and piety, and was revered by the people of Egypt.
